correctness.rationale: For arbitrary real-linear extensions on Lip(V)/constants, signed-permutation averaging is norm nonincreasing. The stabilizer of a facet center has exactly two vertex orbits with signed total weights a+b=1. Coordinate-deletion distance data are 1-Lipschitz, have equal facet means S_N on both orbits, and vanish at a face vertex distance sqrt(N) from its center. Thus every extension costs at least S_N/sqrt(N). The positive face-averaging operator has exhaustive pair-orbit costs: vertex/vertex=1, same-face vertex/center=S_N/sqrt(N), opposite-face vertex/center=U_N/sqrt(N+4), any two centers=1. The inequality U_N/sqrt(N+4)<=S_N/sqrt(N) is proved for N>=4 using variance and Jensen (an exact nonnegative rational difference) and for N=2,3 via explicit radical comparisons. Strict monotonicity follows from leave-one-out conditional Jensen; the limit and 1/N term follow from binomial moments. All hypotheses, signs, all integer dimensions d>=3, and exact Euclidean normalization are accounted for. The independent standard-library script tested 7,152 vertex-center pairs and 365 center-center pairs in d=3..8; finite tests were not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full relevant material of Bruè–Di Marino–Stra (arXiv:1801.07533) and Basso (arXiv:2310.13554) concerns general extension constructions and bounds, without an exact simultaneous Euclidean facet-center theorem. A highly pertinent previously indexed cube-center result determines the single-center optimum and thus provides a lower bound after restricting to one facet, but its accessible statement does not supply simultaneous compatibility at all 2d centers or the off-facet vertex inequality; no implication of the present full statement was found. Accessible earlier cube edge-midpoint and simplex face-barycenter claims refer to different added sets and do not imply this result. Detailed published-finding corpus and literature searches did not locate a covering statement. Full text of the cube-center record was inaccessible; unindexed equivalent results remain a residual originality risk. This is qualified scientific best-knowledge originality, not a uniqueness claim.

value.rationale: The configuration of all Euclidean hypercube facet centers is a canonical simultaneous finite metric trace/refinement problem. The theorem precisely identifies an intrinsic least linear Lipschitz extension norm and shows that simple positive face averaging achieves the full unrestricted optimum despite arbitrary signed, asymmetric, all-vertex competitors. Existing one-face lower bounds do not ensure consistency among all 2d centers: new pair-orbit compatibility and the off-facet inequality overcome that obstruction. The strict dimension growth and sharp approach to sqrt(2) show a nontrivial structural law with a reusable cubical interpolation benchmark. It is not an arbitrary isolated finite number, a textbook deduction from the center case, or a small unmotivated improvement.
